purpose: two repairs to the v1.05 contract arm: a token cap the degenerate model can finish inside, and a control family that can express the shape the model used
follows: experiments/v105/spec (the E6 arm: 10/83 vs 6/83, 7/83 vs 6/83 above the retained-volume floor, p = 1, verdict: no net contribution)

max_tokens.because: deepseek-v4.1-flash-ark returned empty content in 207 of 249 units at 1500 and hit the cap in 208. Same repair as the v1.04 atom arm (6000 -> 16k), and the same consequence: this arm cannot be compared to the other two on call cost.

control_family.now: the same grid, plus every single-parameter half at cut points (midpoint, 0, 1, -1), merged into one list ordered by descending retained volume; largest box that proves wins
control_family.because: the two cases the model won in v1.05 -- gj2007b (`n in [1, 2^31-1]`) and half (`k in [-1e6, -1]`) -- are single-parameter signs splits. A family that cannot write them has not lost to structure.

primary_pairing.was: best of 3 repeats, union over 3 models
primary_pairing.because: best-of-3 and any-model are extra samples the control never got; both are still reported, as sensitivities.

material_floor.now: ladder (0.0, 1e-05, 0.0001, 0.001, 0.01, 0.1, 0.25, 0.5), verdict must hold at every rung
material_floor.because: 1e-3 discards the sharpest answers on this benchmark (the correct box for `n*n` is 2.2e-5 of the domain). Moving a constant after seeing the data is the failure this audit documents; requiring the sign to survive a ladder is not.

control_exceptions.was: folded into UNKNOWN, disclosed in prose
control_exceptions.now: own column; a case is ERROR only if every attempt raised

population: the 83 programs of the v1.05 contract arm, re-derived and compared element by element against that protocol's own case list (corpus, name, bounds, source hash, translation hash). 101 llmloop units of the two v1.04 studies were unproved at declared bounds and translated by the frozen front end; 18 have no interval of positive width and are listed under no_room. Labels: 14 true, 69 false. The control family needs at most 35 attempts per case (11 uniform rungs + 8 halves per parameter of positive width, 3 of them at most).
task: one call: the model states a box on the parameters; the frozen pipeline is re-run inside it; the outcome is conditional on the box and reported with the retained fraction. Same prompt, same system message, same temperature as v1.05.
control: model-free search over the pre-registered family in `family()`: 11 uniform rungs plus single-parameter halves, in descending retained volume, first proof wins. Budget 900 s per case against the model arm's 600 s per verify, and up to 35 attempts against the model arm's one call: both asymmetries favour the control, which is the direction a control should be biased in.
decision_rule: per case, the contract arm proves a case if its first repeat does; the control if any box in its family does. At each floor t in (0.0, 1e-05, 0.0001, 0.001, 0.01, 0.1, 0.25, 0.5), pair the two arms on the 83 cases and compute exact McNemar over the discordant pairs. The contract arm is credited with a capability only if, at EVERY rung where either arm claims anything, only-S exceeds only-B with p < 0.05. A single rung where that fails kills the claim, so no choice of t can produce it. Masked reachable overflow (a false-labelled case "proved" under a box) is counted, never treated as success.
prompt_source: scripts/spec_v105.py:prompt -- imported, not copied, and hashed above
pipeline: llmloop.houdini_loops, integer_model=c, runs=60, max_rounds=150, solver_timeout_ms=5000, seed=1, default profile then the polynomial profile

driver_amendments.change: After the first dispatch answered 18 of 249 calls and then got HTTP 403 `Insufficient user quota` for the rest, three defects in this driver were fixed: a refused call was recorded as MALFORMED (a capability column) instead of NOT_ANSWERED; the summary then computed 'empty replies 233/249' over units that were never answered and called the arm degenerate, which is the v1.05 mistake at a larger scale; and 249 calls could be dispatched without asking whether the account could answer. Added: `NOT_ANSWERED` as a status, `reclassify()` so the merge re-derives it from `raw/<i>/call.json` instead of trusting an old row, a void banner with `verdict_applicable: false`, and a `preflight` subcommand the workflow now runs before the shards.
driver_amendments.why_the_freeze_moved: The freeze was regenerated after the run so that the next dispatch can run at all: `run` refuses to execute under a freeze whose source hashes do not match the tree, which is the gate doing its job. The bytes that produced the rows in this directory are recorded in `protocol_sha256_used`, and `results.json` writes that hash, not the current one -- so the mismatch between `protocol_sha256_used` and sha256(protocol.json) is the visible, checkable statement that these rows predate the freeze that is on disk now. No row in this directory was produced by the code this protocol froze. The freeze was regenerated a second time, for the same reason and with the same consequence: the void banner had to learn to say that the protocol above it postdates the rows, and that edit landed after the first regeneration.
driver_amendments.to_rerun: a new dispatch after the balance is restored; `preflight` will refuse it in one call if the account still cannot answer

driver_amendments.change: Three reporting defects, no arm logic: (1) the summary took `sorted(xs)[len(xs)//2]` as a median, which is the upper middle value for even n -- on the 18 answers (159..16384 tokens) it printed 7,558 where the median is 5,784, and that number had already been carried into a cost projection; (2) the cost table divided 7,689 prompt tokens and 110,400 completion tokens by 249 requests although only 18 answers carry a usage block, i.e. 31 tokens per call, and it labelled 1,363 s of wall clock as generation time when 745 s of it was retry backoff on refused calls; (3) `completion_tokens_details.reasoning_tokens` was never recorded, so the claim 'the 1500 cap truncated reasoning' was prose. Added a real median, a `reasoning_tokens` column (filled from `raw/*/call.json` on merge for rows that predate it), separate request/answer denominators, and a cost projection stated as the range its two statistics give.
driver_amendments.why_the_freeze_moved: `run` refuses a freeze whose source hashes do not match the tree, and it cannot tell a reporting edit from a treatment edit. So the freeze moves again, and the rows in this directory stay attached to `protocol_sha256_used` (1d209c7b...), not to the bytes now on disk: the banner at the top of summary.md is the checkable statement that they predate it. Freeze regenerated twice before for the same reason; this is the third and it is the same lesson -- a summary function is not a neutral observer of the run it summarises.
driver_amendments.to_rerun: a new dispatch after the balance is restored; `preflight` refuses it in one call if the account still cannot answer
